title: Rare pregnancy infections may triple the risk of autism

title: Why Viking museums still can’t escape the warrior myth

title: Black holes of every size follow the same surprising rule

Supermassive black holes can produce jets soon after tearing apart a star, then fire up again hundreds or thousands of days later when their feeding rate drops to about 2% of the Eddington limit. That same threshold is known to trigger jets from much smaller black holes in the Milky Way.

title: A new process turns plastic waste into gasoline and diesel fuel

title: Scientists create a needle-thin brain implant that can do three jobs at once
